subject: general
question: Albert Bourla, winner of the Genesis Prize 2022, is the CEO of which of the following companies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pfizer Inc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pfizer chief Albert Bourla**

 
 
• Albert Bourla, **Chairman and CEO **of the multinational pharmaceutical company **Pfizer Inc**., received the prestigious **Genesis Prize 2022 on January 19, 2022**.
 
• He received recognition for his work overseeing the creation of the **Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine**.
 
• Each year, a recipient of the **$1 million** award is recognised for their professional accomplishments, humanitarian efforts, and dedication to Jewish ideals.
 
• According to the Genesis Prize Foundation, **Mr Bourla won the most votes during an online voting process that involved almost 200,000 participants from 71 different countries**.
 
• Dr. Bourla requested that The Genesis Prize Foundation utilise his $1 million award **to create a Holocaust museum in Thessaloniki, Greece, where he was born**.
 
• The **"Jewish Nobel Prize" i**s how people commonly refer to it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Jewish Agency Chairman's Office (a nonprofit organisation with strong ties to the Israeli government) and the private Genesis Prize Foundation, jointly administer the prize, which was established in 2014**.
 
• A **$100 million endowment **created for it provides the funding for this prize.
 
• According to the organisation, the **Greek-born Bourla, who is the son of Holocaust survivors**, wishes to contribute his award money to programs focused on preserving the memory of Holocaust victims, particularly in Greece.
 
• Pfizer's partner, **BioNTech, secured funds from the German government**, and Pfizer subsequently signed a major supply agreement with the United States.
 
• The strategy placed** Pfizer in the frontline of international efforts to fight the coronavirus**, and its **vaccine was the first to be approved** for use in **the United States and Europe**.
